reviewPurpose: Adversarial design review of kinetic architecture v1.0.0, focused on common-cause failures, failure containment, service human factors, dynamic-test evidence and conditions that must remain open before a released kinetic mechanism is possible.

designReviewFindings.finding: A holding or fault brake acting only through the gearbox and belt/gear transmission can share the same failure path as the drive transmission. A broken or disengaged transmission can therefore remove both propulsion and the through-drive holding path.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Evaluate and qualify a fixed-side brake acting directly on a passive carrier brake ring/disc, or another demonstrably independent carrier holding path. A motor/gearbox brake may remain supplemental but cannot by itself close transmission-failure containment.

designReviewFindings.finding: The annular secondary-retention concept can still have a common-cause weakness if its rotating capture feature depends on the same local hub, fasteners or fractured carrier region whose failure it is intended to contain.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Develop a fault-coverage matrix and distributed carrier capture attachments that bypass relevant primary-bearing rings/bolts and do not rely on one local hub feature. State explicitly which carrier structural failures are and are not contained.

designReviewFindings.finding: Using one motion feedback source for closed-loop control, stall detection and overspeed creates a common-mode blind spot if that source fails plausibly.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Define an independent or sufficiently diverse speed/overspeed plausibility channel if required by risk assessment. Passive rotating targets remain preferred so no rotating power is introduced.

designReviewFindings.finding: Brake-fails-to-release and brake-fails-to-apply are materially different faults but were not separately controlled.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Require brake-state verification where practical, distinguish release/apply failure diagnostics, and prohibit access based only on a brake command without verified zero motion and mechanical lock.

designReviewFindings.finding: Manual brake or gearbox release can create unintended free motion from residual imbalance, suspended-field restoring effects or external disturbance.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Manual recovery must require verified zero speed, positive service lock engagement before release of the normal holding path, controlled two-action release and a procedure that never creates an uncontrolled freewheel condition.

designReviewFindings.finding: Soft start and soft stop are necessary but not specific enough for a 240-pendulum field. Acceleration discontinuities and jerk can excite the field even when peak acceleration is low.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Use a jerk-limited or equivalently smooth command profile as the preferred control study and derive acceleration, jerk and settling dwell from T1-T4 physical measurements.

designReviewFindings.finding: The rigid-body polar-inertia calculation is useful for screening but does not represent the full transient coupling of long suspended masses that lag the carrier during acceleration and braking.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Treat rigid-body inertia as a calculation bound/input only and correlate drive/brake demand against measured suspended-field response. Do not close torque sizing solely from m*r^2 mass mapping.

designReviewFindings.finding: Bearing selection requirements did not make the mounting-structure flatness, circumferential rigidity, fastener preload verification and post-assembly running-torque check explicit enough.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Make manufacturer mounting tolerances and bolt/preload procedure controlled selection inputs and verify mounted running torque/runout before dynamic field testing.

designReviewFindings.finding: Belt pretension or gear mesh reactions can add radial load and local frame distortion even at very low carrier speed.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Feed transmission pretension, tangential force and tensioner reactions into bearing/support calculations and verify that the drive mount does not distort the bearing support ring.

designReviewFindings.finding: Stopped, held, mechanically locked and safe-to-access states were not encoded as distinct operator states.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Release a commissioning/service state model with explicit transitions, permissives and direct physical lock verification. Fault reset must never itself command motion.

designReviewFindings.finding: Noise is a primary product goal but no controlled acoustic acceptance method or acceptance criterion exists yet.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Define measurement positions, background-noise method, operating states and acceptance criterion only after prototype baseline and project/product requirements are available.

designReviewFindings.finding: An endurance duty and re-inspection interval cannot be inferred from slow rpm alone. Brake cycles, starts/stops, bearing rotations, belt/gear cycles, service-lock cycles and sensor drift have different duty measures.
designReviewFindings.requiredDisposition: Define an evidence-based duty spectrum and endurance plan before release, followed by teardown/inspection criteria that can inform maintenance intervals.

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: primary bearing rolling-element/race/internal support failure causing abnormal axial separation or tilt
detectionRequirements: abnormal motion/runout or speed response where detectable
requiredMechanicalContainment: normally-clear fixed catch sectors engage distributed rotating capture features
load transfers to fixed structural frame and valid site interfaces
system remains out of service after any engagement

detectionRequirements: runout/play or contact anomaly where detectable
requiredMechanicalContainment: secondary retention must bypass the failed bearing fastener load path
capture brackets must load the fixed structural frame through independent attachment regions

detectionRequirements: unexpected runout/vibration/contact if developed during operation
requiredMechanicalContainment: distributed capture attachments must not all depend on the same fractured local hub feature
uncontained structural failure modes must be explicitly listed and controlled by primary structural design
evidenceRequired: representative proof test or justified analysis

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: positive belt tooth/belt body/ring interface or gear transmission failure
requiredMechanicalContainment: carrier holding/fault-stop capability cannot rely only on the failed transmission
evaluate fixed-side spring-applied brake acting directly on passive carrier brake ring/disc or justified equivalent
remove propulsion
qualified carrier stop/holding path
no automatic restart

detectionRequirements: drive load rise with no carrier motion
requiredMechanicalContainment: abort start without escalating drive torque indefinitely
remain stopped
require fault disposition before restart

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: holding/fault brake fails to apply or loses holding force
requiredMechanicalContainment: do not permit mechanical access
service lock may engage only after independently verified zero speed
maintenance procedure treats failed brake as unreleased stored-motion hazard

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: primary position/speed feedback loss, frozen value or plausible corruption
detectionRequirements: independent/diverse motion plausibility channel where required
requiredMechanicalContainment: transition to defined fault stop
no automatic motion restart

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: service lock partial engagement, false indication or attempted motion while engaged
requiredMechanicalContainment: captive lock geometry prevents inadvertent withdrawal
drive cannot intentionally run with lock engaged
lock receiver designed for defined proof loads without using bearing rolling elements as the restraint

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: secondary retention contacts during normal operation due runout, tolerance stack, frame deflection or loosened component
requiredMechanicalContainment: stop and remove from service
no intentional rubbing or load sharing in normal operation

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: trim mass or rotating service hardware loosens
requiredMechanicalContainment: trim masses positively locked and secondarily captured
no loose hardware can enter field or fixed/rotating interface
controlled or fault stop according to validated condition
do not repeatedly auto-retry into the obstruction

faultContainmentMatrix.initiatingFailure: site power loss or kinetic-domain isolation while rotating
detectionRequirements: carrier speed verification after control power returns
requiredMechanicalContainment: propulsion removed
power-off holding/stopping function acts without requiring rotating electrical power
no automatic restart after power returns
evidenceRequired: power interruption tests across released speeds/load cases

braking.preferredStudy: fixed-side spring-applied, electrically released caliper or equivalent acts directly on a passive carrier brake ring/disc so parking/fault holding need not pass through the drive belt/gear transmission
braking.motorOrGearboxBrakeRole: supplemental drive/normal-stop support only until an approved failure analysis proves otherwise
braking.serviceLockRole: still mandatory for mechanical access; direct carrier brake does not replace the positive service lock

secondaryRetention.preferredStudy: multiple fixed catch sectors and multiple distributed rotating capture attachments connected to carrier structural regions independent of relevant primary-bearing fasteners/rings

feedback.primaryChannel: fixed non-contact carrier position/speed readhead with passive rotating target
feedback.overspeedStudy: evaluate an independent or sufficiently diverse fixed-side speed plausibility channel; exact architecture follows risk assessment and fault-detection latency

motionProfile.preferredCommandShape: jerk-limited S-curve or physically equivalent smooth profile
motionProfile.restartAfterStop: test-derived settling dwell or other validated settled-state criterion before reversal/restart where needed

requirements: supplier-controlled mounting flatness and support rigidity
full-circumference support where required by selected family
post-mount running torque and runout verification
bearingMounting.driveInterfaceRule: belt/gear/tensioner reactions and frame distortion are included in bearing/support load cases

manualRecovery.rule: no manual release creates an uncontrolled freewheel condition
sequencePrinciple: engage and directly verify positive service lock
only then use controlled manual brake/drive release if procedure requires
restore normal holding path before removing service lock

dynamicCalculation.requiredCorrelation: physical drive/brake load and suspended-field lag measurements at T1-T4 must correlate or correct the calculation model before torque selection approval
